notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/checkboxgroup.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/checkboxgroup.md at e7ed622, the same files on main and docs-next. The guide's Sources note was checked on 28 October 2026 on the 27 October build, and the evidence's top section (“dbe0e02 publish”, 28 October, #357) names it: mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02, Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, the installed build. So items citing the Sources note or that section carry 2026-10-28 and 0.1.78-dbe0e02. The evidence's older sections (Checked, Sources, Contract, Rendered, Limits, Verification) are from 28 September on jfs-components 0.1.60; no item cites them. Installed CheckboxGroup.tsx (dbe0e02) matches every guide sentence used here, read from source with token values through the package's own getVariableByName, not rendered: the props are children, modes, style and accessibilityLabel (lines 8–23); the group is a View with width 100%, a column, align stretch, gap checkboxGroup/gap 12 and padding checkboxGroup/padding 0 × 0, the same with no modes, Color Mode Dark, Context ListItem and any Slot gap (51–64); with children it clones each one with its modes, without children it renders three CheckboxItems (66–74), whose default label is “Fixed deposit • 0245” and default checked false (CheckboxItem.tsx 137, 163), so three identical unchecked rows; the group is role list named by accessibilityLabel and nothing else (77–81). Each CheckboxItem clones its end-slot child with the modes it got, so the group's modes reach the end-slot Button (CheckboxItem.tsx 294–306). A row is a Pressable with role checkbox, aria-checked, and Space toggling on the web; its inner Checkbox has focusable false, so it is role none, tabIndex −1 and aria-hidden (CheckboxItem.tsx 246–255, 308–323; Checkbox.tsx 236–258): one checkbox and one Tab stop per row, as the Sources note says. A string label is 14/19, weight 400, rgb(13,13,15); the checkbox is 18 px, so a plain row is 19 px tall and three rows in a 272 px column are 272 × 81, the guide's measure. Disabled: the box's stroke goes from rgb(102,102,102) to rgb(153,153,153), and a checked box's fill from rgb(92,0,181) to rgb(219,207,255); the label colour is checkboxItem/foreground in every state (the guide's “The checkbox dims but the label stays the same colour”). Contradicted by the installed build and left out: nothing in the guide; the evidence's 0.1.60 lines (duplicated checkbox roles, no aria-checked, Space not toggling) are what its dbe0e02 section replaces. Not recorded: style (the building rules keep style overrides off Coin components); the Figma row height (18 px against 19 px installed), a Figma detail the guide reports only as a difference from the package; the 0.1.60 Contract's list of what the group lacks (selection, select-all, validation, error, heading, orientation), which the guide states as the screen's job instead (the screen supplies the heading and owns the checked state; the group does not limit or count selections) and which would cite 0.1.60 lines; the Storybook's stories (the guide lists five; no age of the published Storybook is recorded). The guide names no component to use instead for a single choice, so that avoidWhen rule has no useInstead. Anatomy: all four parts are always present: the group always renders rows, its own or three placeholders, and every CheckboxItem renders a checkbox and a label unless a label of null or false is passed. Strength: “The group accepts Checkbox Items only.” is required, everywhere, like Tab Item's “Always place a Tab Item inside Tabs”; the package types accept any node (CheckboxItem or compatible elements), so the rule is the guide's, not a type. Three other quotes hold “only” as a description of the group or a limit on when to disable, recorded with their reasons. content.bad is empty: the Don'ts' copy is not bad copy in itself (“Send me offers by SMS” is wrong among accounts, “Monthly” and “Yearly” are wrong as checkboxes); the rules say so. Gaps: the rows sit in the group's list without list items (dbe0e02 section, still so in the installed source), a leftover of #357, which closed with it; no open ticket covers it that this run could see. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode anywhere (the guide sets Light on the Card, the Button, the heading and every group). The guide's source sets Button / Size XS on every group (GROUP_MODES), which its copy never mentions; it matters only where a row has an end action: the default Button is Size M (20 px side padding, a 16 px label that neither wraps nor shrinks), wider than the 80 px end slot for “Manage”, and the Checkbox Item entry's rule records XS through the row's modes so the Button fits. So the end-action example sets Button / Size XS on the group, which forwards it to every item and end-slot child, and the other two set no modes. Rows are controlled, as the guide's In context has the screen own each item's checked state: checked comes from the screen, and onValueChange stands for the screen's own wiring, which stores the new value and passes it back. The In context example is the screen as it first shows: nothing selected and the Button disabled with “Select an account”; the guide's source relabels it “Link 1 account” or “Link N accounts” once something is selected. Copy is the guide's own. Card and Text have undocumented entries in this pack; Link, Button and CheckboxItem have guide entries. Left out of examples (three at most): Plain labels on their own (In context shows them), Mixed selection, Disabled rows (the guide's shows no reason beside the disabled rows, which the Checkbox Item entry asks for), the sizing columns, the Do & Don'ts and the playground. Sorting (batch 10, rounds 1–3): round 1 found five flags. Three were our misreadings, all fixed: the empty-group rule said “never ship”, stronger than the guide's Do & Don't; a content rule turned the Pass real items caption (“Each row names a real account”) into a rule for every group (removed; the configuration rule keeps Pass real items); and the In context purpose quoted “Link 1 account”, which is in the guide's source but not on the page (removed). /configuration/7 also now cites only its own sentence, with the states sentence as its own rule. Round 2 found one more of ours, fixed: the rule that the screen enables its button read as a rule for every group (now the guide's Choose accounts to link screen); its notes also led to dropping “above the group” from the heading rule and the purpose's “no row here has an end action”. Rounds 1–3 flagged /examples/1 (the row's accessibilityLabel and the Link's autolayout Hug) and /examples/2 (Button / Size XS on the group): both are in the guide's source (lines 8, 17–18, 56), which the cross-check can't see, so round 3's flags are dismissed in reviews/checkboxgroup.json. Round 3's note that content.good mixes the Email, SMS and Push notification options (from the Do & Don't) with account labels is left as it is (a fourth run is not allowed); for Astra to decide.

examples.purpose: Choose accounts to link, the guide's In context, as the screen first shows it: a Card with the screen's heading in a Text, the group named by accessibilityLabel, and the Button. The screen owns each row's checked value: onValueChange stands for the screen's own wiring, which stores the new value and passes it back as checked. The screen enables the Button once something is selected; onPress stands for linking. It sets no modes.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <Text text="Choose accounts to link" />
  <CheckboxGroup accessibilityLabel="Accounts to link">
    <CheckboxItem checked={false} onValueChange={(checked) => {}}>Fixed deposit • 0245</CheckboxItem>
    <CheckboxItem checked={false} onValueChange={(checked) => {}}>Recurring deposit • 1182</CheckboxItem>
    <CheckboxItem checked={false} onValueChange={(checked) => {}}>Mutual fund • Equity</CheckboxItem>
    <CheckboxItem checked={false} onValueChange={(checked) => {}}>Savings account • 4821</CheckboxItem>
  </CheckboxGroup>
  <Button label="Select an account" disabled onPress={() => {}} />
</Card>

from.quote: The screen supplies the heading, owns each item’s checked state, and enables the button once something is selected.
